translations.literal: Later they again altered the three procession hymns used during ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Later they again altered the three ceremonial procession poems.

units.zh: 第一日《於赫篇》，詠武帝，聲節與古《鹿鳴》同。

translations.literal: The first they titled “How Radiant”—praising Emperor Wu—its rhythm matched the ancient “Deer Call.”
translations.idiomatic: Piece one, “How Radiant,” hymned Emperor Wu to the old meter of “Deer Call.”

units.zh: 第二曰《巍巍篇》，詠文帝，用延年所改《騶虞》聲。

translations.literal: The second they titled “How Towering”—praising Emperor Wen—using the sound Zuo Yannian had refashioned for “Zouyu.”
translations.idiomatic: Piece two, “How Towering,” praised Emperor Wen with Zuo Yannian’s revised “Zouyu” tune.

translations.literal: Flowing fortune shines—displayed through myriad ages.
translations.idiomatic: Streaming mandate gleams—visible across endless succession.

translations.literal: Radiant royal ancestor—winging ages, aiding seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Radiant illustrious ancestor—supporting eras, steadying hours.

translations.literal: He quieted six coordinates—received mandate matching its season.
translations.idiomatic: He stilled all six realms—answered Heaven’s scheduled charge.

translations.literal: He opened imperial thoroughfare—thereby completing emperor’s foundation.
translations.idiomatic: He cleared royal highway—thus sealed imperial groundwork.

translations.literal: Bright, bright Emperor Jing—none rival his fiery merit.
translations.idiomatic: Luminous Emperor Jing—no competitor matches his blazing deed.

translations.literal: He corrected age and rescued vulgar ways—rest merit blankets ages.
translations.idiomatic: He righted the hour and salvaged coarse custom—restorative glory roofs eternity.

translations.literal: Heaven’s mandate descended watchful—it opened fortune for wise clarity.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven dropped inspecting charge—it unlocked luck for enlightened rule.

translations.literal: Solemn fierce Father—both discerning and outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: Grave martial father—clarifying and brilliant alike.

translations.literal: Truly Heaven bore his virtue—he answered spirit-driven fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven truly bred his power—he matched numinous revolution.

translations.literal: Heaven mantles manifest stipend—fortunate tread rests soothed.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven drapes bright salary—lucky footing stays eased.

translations.literal: Radiant Grand Progenitor—he enlarged bright virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Blazing Founding Father—he widened lucid power.

translations.literal: He opened cosmic halls—corrected age and planted norms.
translations.idiomatic: He unrolled universe—righted era and set patterns.

units.zh: 及武帝受命之初，百度草創。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu first received Heaven’s charge, every regulation was still rough-hewn.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset of Emperor Wu’s receiving the mandate, institutions existed only in embryo.

units.zh: 泰始二年，詔郊祀明堂禮樂權用魏儀，遵周室肇稱殷禮之義，但改樂章而已，使傅玄為之詞雲。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taishi an edict declared that suburban rites, the Bright Hall, ritual, and music should provisionally follow Wei ceremony—honoring Zhou’s precedent of initially labeling rituals Yin—except that hymn texts alone were replaced, assigning Fu Xuan to compose the lyrics.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taishi an edict ordered suburban and Bright Hall liturgy to borrow Wei forms—echoing Zhou’s habit of calling early rituals Shang-style—while swapping only the hymn lyrics, commissioned from Fu Xuan.
